title: VacationResponse singleton enforcement at handler level is correct design
description: vacation.rs: create/destroy are rejected with SetErrorType::Singleton at the handler, not at the backend. This is correct: the singleton invariant is a protocol rule that the backend should not have to enforce. The upsert logic (update singleton that doesn't exist yet → create then re-apply patch) handles the initialization case cleanly. A contributor might suggest moving singleton enforcement to the backend trait; that would be wrong because it would require every backend implementation to duplicate the protocol rule.
